sites.match: GitHub op ${githubOp} refused under every grant

guards.invariant: an omp github call whose op is not one of omp's read ops never runs under any task grant
guards.source: the op argument of the github call, checked by refusedGithubOp in bin/fm-jev-egress.ts against the read ops installed omp 18.12.6 approves as reads (repo_view, file_read, search_issues, search_prs, search_code, search_commits, search_repos, run_watch)
guards.trigger: refusedGithubOp(<input>) finds a github op outside those read ops, such as pr_checkout, pr_create or pr_push, which write worktrees, branches, git config, refs or the remote, or an unknown, non-string or missing op

guards.fail_direction_note: an op that is missing, not a string or not a recognized read op is refused; the read-op list is compiled into the guard module; a runtime that cannot load it is denied in an active project scope and, per docs/configuration.md Jev guard, does not block in an inactive project scope
guards.telemetry_note: each github call emits one event through bin/fm-guard-event.sh into state/guard-events.jsonl with the guard id, decision (allow for a read op, deny for any other op), source_ok and elapsed time only, keyed to session <task>:github-read for an allow and <task>:github-write for a deny, so a read op never counts as clearing a write-op refusal, which nothing clears; a read op then still meets jev-egress-grant; the content-free terminal row in state/jev-guard.jsonl remains the task audit

guards.invariant: a task commit never adds a line holding a known credential shape
guards.source: lines git diff --cached adds against HEAD and every MERGE_HEAD parent, after the repository pre-commit hook, net of lines the same diff removes, matched against the anchored shapes in bin/fm-git-secrets.py
guards.trigger: an added staged line holds a private-key header, a GitHub, AWS access key or Slack token prefix shape, or a connection URL with an embedded password of 8 or more characters
guards.remedy: remove the credential from the named files, restage them with git add <file>, and rerun git commit; python3 bin/fm-git-secrets.py pre-commit replays the check against the index
guards.layer_note: per-task wrappers installed by bin/fm-git-strip-ai-trailers.sh: pre-commit scans after the repository hook; pre-push scans before replaying the ref-update input to it. Every repository is checked, but only decisions in the task worktree record events. A refusal repeats only while the same new credential-shaped line, identified by its content hash, is refused in consecutive decisions. Different refused content starts at 1 even after an abandoned attempt. A failed inspection counts as its own episode under a reserved inspection-failed key and keeps the per-line counts; only an allowed decision clears the counts. Each refusal past the budget of 1 also prints an escalation to a human decision, and the operation stays refused. The shared Python deny decision and refusal messages are mapped once under git-commit-credential-shapes; GUARDS selects the pre-commit or pre-push telemetry id at runtime, so this source ownership also covers the push path without two registry entries claiming one site.

guards.invariant: a runaway status log never fills the disk or stalls the readers that walk it
guards.source: the byte size and line count of the status log or span, measured in bin/fm-status-cap-lib.sh against the cap and reserve (FM_STATUS_CAP_BYTES, FM_STATUS_CAP_RESERVE_BYTES), plus whether the path given to bin/fm-status-append.sh is a symbolic link
guards.trigger: an append through bin/fm-status-append.sh would pass the 33554432-byte cap (cap plus the 1048576-byte reserve for a decision or terminal line), a reader asks for a span past cap plus reserve or, line by line, past 32768 lines, or the append path is a symbolic link
guards.remedy: read the latest events with tail -c 4194304 state/<task>.status, or retire the log by tearing the lane down with bin/fm-teardown.sh <task>
guards.layer_note: added by PR #188 after a status-append loop filled the disk; deny without a guard event: an append past the cap exits 75 and a refused read returns status 2, each naming the file on stderr, and nothing is written or read; the symbolic-link refusal keeps the capped append on the status log itself; bin/fm-status-cap-guard.sh raises the over-cap wake for a raw writer; docs/configuration.md "Status log size bounds" describes the bounds for operators; the test proves the cap and both read refusals, and the symbolic-link refusal has no fixture

guards.invariant: a Slack retarget never drops answers or notices still pending on the old DM
guards.source: the pending journal in state/slack-watch/state.json, read by Watch.retarget() in bin/fm_slack_watch.py against the owner id stored for the established DM and FM_SLACK_DM_USER
guards.trigger: bin/fm-slack-check.sh retarget runs after FM_SLACK_DM_USER changed while the pending journal still holds an answer or a notice for a thread in the old DM, or when the retarget's own read of an old thread stages one
guards.remedy: restore the old FM_SLACK_DM_USER in .env, run bin/fm-slack-poll.sh until python3 -c 'import json; print(len(json.load(open("state/slack-watch/state.json"))["pending"]))' prints 0, set the new value, then run bin/fm-slack-check.sh disarm, bin/fm-slack-check.sh retarget, bin/fm-slack-check.sh arm; last resort, when a pending row can never drain because its thread or channel is gone: run bin/fm-slack-check.sh disarm, check the pending rows by hand, then remove state/slack-watch/ to start a fresh DM, which can re-read replies that were already answered; the same last resort covers an old thread that retarget can never read or judge (a hold id that can never be probed, a tapper whose users.info lookup keeps failing, a deleted card): first read that thread in Slack by hand and record any answer with bin/fm-captain-hold.sh answer, then disarm and remove state/slack-watch/, which abandons that thread's unread reply
guards.layer_note: added by the Slack watch activation-readiness change; deny without a guard event: retarget exits non-zero with slack: refused: dm_user_changed_with_pending_work (raised in Watch.retarget in bin/fm_slack_watch.py) and changes the journal only by the rows its own read of the old threads staged; without the guard, answers pending on the old DM would be lost or misrouted after a retarget; the two bin/fm-slack-check.sh help lines document the refusal and its remedy; test X26 proves the refusal on a journal that already holds work and the retarget that succeeds once the journal is empty; test X41 proves the refusal after the retarget read stages an unread reply, that only that row is added, and the retarget that succeeds once it drains
